title: [epic] Studio design surface layout redesign: one skeleton for the shell and the four pillars (Data, Automations, Interfaces, Access), from the 2026-10-15 design canvas
body:
## Source

The Studio design surface (`/_console/studio/app.objectstack.hotcrm/data` (the package id, then the pillar segment), `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and its panels) is the console's metadata-authoring workbench. On 2026-10-15 the maintainer reviewed it in the browser against the HotCRM app (objectui main `a2225f91`, hotcrm served by `objectstack serve --dev`) and asked for a layout redesign: the pillars stack a shell header, a pillar-specific second band, an object header that spans the rail, a segmented tab strip and a bordered card before the first row of content; read-only is said in five places; the Automations rail is a flat list of 23 flows; the Interfaces rail shows one kind of entry at a time.

The target is a design canvas of eight artboards (a Claude Design artifact, private to the maintainer): Data Records (writable), Data Form designer, Data Records (read-only package), Automations, Access, Interfaces page designer, Interfaces object entry, Interfaces dashboard entry. Every child card below restates its artboard in words and numbers, so a developer never needs the canvas.

## Session

Epic PM session: `session_cdb7a717-def7-4e71-9988-f089fbaa18ff` (Claude Code desktop, maintainer attending).

## Territory

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/**` — `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (shell, DataPillar, AutomationsPillar, InterfacesPillar, AccessPillar), `ObjectFormDesigner.tsx`, `ObjectListViewInspector.tsx`, and two new shared files the children introduce (a rail and an inspector shell).
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — Studio keys only (`engine.studio.*`, `engine.inspector.appNav.*`).
- Named but not claimed: `packages/plugin-grid` (the Records toolbar's icon-only buttons) — the Data card touches it only if the toolbar restyle cannot be done from the host.
- Outside the subtree: the objectstack console pin bump (`pnpm objectui:refresh` + manifest regeneration) is a follow-up card in objectstack-ai/objectstack once the last child lands. The Console Pin Gate builds and does not boot, so that bump opens the console locally and walks all four pillars.

## Rulings

Maintainer, in this session on 2026-10-15, verbatim:

> 使用 pm-dispatch 技能，创建专题卡，以及具体的子卡片。

> 流程自动化左侧平铺有点乱，是否建议按对象分类？

> 界面设计那个你看一下真实的前端界面，而且有很多种菜单类型，仪表盘只是一种。

Design decisions the canvas carries, which every child cites by number:

1. **One skeleton for all four pillars.** Rail 240 px → content column (item header row + underline tab row + toolbar + body) → inspector aside 300 px. The pillar-specific second band (Automations "Off by default · review before enabling", Interfaces "Home · Dashboard", Access "Permission matrix · Objects × CRUD") retires; what it said moves into the item header row of the content column.
2. **Shell header, 48 px, a three-column grid.** Left: home, then an app chip (24 px app icon tile, package name, chevron). Center: the pillars as a segmented control. Right: Changes with a count badge, Publish. The "·" separator retires.
3. **Type scale and rhythm.** 18 / 13 / 12 / 11 px for item title / body / meta / label; rail rows 32 px, table rows 40 px, radius 8 px; the console's existing primary token; no new colors.
4. **Read-only is said twice.** A lock with "Read-only" in the app chip, and one "Read-only · Customize with an overlay" link in the item header. Publish drops to an outline disabled button; the rail's add button hides; "Add record" stays because records remain usable.
5. **Rails carry the user's mental model.** Automations groups by trigger object; Interfaces shows the app's navigation tree exactly as the shipped sidebar renders it, and "+" offers the ten nav kinds the spec declares.

## Open decisions

Three children reverse an earlier ruling or a pinned behavior. Each names it. The maintainer answers here, on this card; until then the three stay unclaimed.

- **A. Access in the nav, More retired** (child: the pillar nav card). objectui#11794 ruled that the More trigger keeps its own name whichever overflow pillar is open; `StudioDesignSurface.moreKeepsName-11794.test.tsx` pins it. The canvas retires More because `OVERFLOW_PILLARS` holds exactly one pillar today, so the menu is a one-item dropdown.
- **B. Advanced flattened** (child: the Data pillar card). The same ruling keeps the Advanced trigger's name; `DataPillar.advancedKeepsName-11794.test.tsx` pins it. The canvas shows seven flat tabs at the 1280 px design width; the card proposes that below roughly 1000 px the overflow returns with its name.
- **C. Access as five tabs** instead of one scrolling page (child: the Access card).

## Children

Posted as a checklist comment on this card once the ten exist; each child carries a `Parent:` line and the shared cards list the pillar cards that depend on them.

## Acceptance (epic)

- Every child merged, each PR carrying before/after screenshots of the same place from the local console (`pnpm --filter @object-ui/console dev`, port 5180) in light and dark.
- The four pillars share the skeleton of decision 1 and the header of decision 2; a screenshot per pillar at 1280 px shows the rail, item header, tab row and aside at the same x and y across all four.
- The follow-up pin bump filed in objectstack-ai/objectstack and linked here.
